description: Agent Healthcare: submit a prescription record with the medication list and the label as dispensed: the prescription with its id, the day written, the prescriber, the medication, strength, form, directions, quantity and refills; optionally each entry of the medication list with its id, medication, strength, directions and status (active, changed or stopped); and optionally the dispensed label with the day dispensed, the pharmacy, the prescriber, the medication, strength, directions, quantity and refills remaining. The signed report gives the prescription, the medication on the label and on the list with the list status, the strength as written, on the label and on the list, the directions on the label and on the list each read as matching or differing, the quantity and refills written and dispensed, and the prescriber on each side, and counts them, and names conflicting records: a label naming another medication, a strength on the label or list unlike the prescription, label directions unlike the prescription, more quantity than written, more refills than written and a medication the list shows as stopped; then a medication missing from the list, list directions unlike the prescription, a prescriber unlike the prescription and a smaller quantity dispensed, with the fix for each and what would change the verdict. No label, no medication list, a strength shown with none written, directions missing on either side, or a quantity or refills shown with none written leaves the prescription unverified. A label dated before the prescription is refused. Directions are read with common label abbreviations spelled out, so 1 tab po bid and 1 tablet by mouth twice daily read as one, and every field is compared as written. This reads the prescription paperwork as transcribed from record to list to label: wever_consent-scope-check reads an agent’s data-use grant against a planned use, not a prescriber’s order, and the Agent Insurance checks read what a policy covers. Verdict health_prescription_conflicting, health_prescription_partial, health_prescription_unverified or health_prescription_consistent. POST /api/health-prescription-check. Reads the care paperwork supplied in the call and returns a signed report with the verdict, the evidence read, the findings with their fixes, and what would change the verdict; it reads paperwork consistency only, with no diagnosis, clinical reading of results, medical necessity judgment or treatment advice, and the paperwork stays in the report, with no network request, fetch, message, payment or external write. Agent Healthcare reads supplied care paperwork after the fact and checks it for consistency against the related records and the summary given to the patient or principal: an itemized bill, a claim as submitted, a prior authorization, a referral, a prescription record and label, a discharge summary, a lab report and an after-visit summary. Beside it, the Agent Insurance checks such as wever_insurance-coverage-check read insurance policies and coverage, what a policy covers, excludes and limits, and where the question is what a policy covers, that is the insurance family’s read, not a healthcare check’s; wever_insurance-evidence-check reads a counterparty’s insurance certificate or policy excerpt for DiligenceOps; wever_callback-health-monitor probes a service’s HTTPS callback endpoint for uptime and reads no care document; and the Agent Consent checks such as wever_consent-scope-check read agent permission and consent records for data handling, not medical consent forms or care documents, while a healthcare check reads no agent permission. Paid URL: 0.10 USDC per call on Base via x402 exact, with the shared 10 signed-wallet free calls per rolling 30 days. Bind X-Wever-Wallet-Proof to the exact JSON arguments and the tool route. Returns a report with an Ed25519 signed receipt. Contract: /api/agent-healthcare-contract. Human page: https://weverlabs.com/agent-healthcare/.
